transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-09-02 15:00 PT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Solaris Head of ML), Ben Marcus (Solaris Platform Eng), Rita Patel (Solaris Security)

Summary (auto): high-level discovery on reliability and incident tolerance for inference. Discussed multi-region routing, fallbacks to smaller/cheaper models, Dedicated warm pool behaviors, and SLA expectations.

Topics: reliability SLOs; failover policies; multi-region and multi-az routing; Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs; private/VPC networking and audit; canary rollouts and health checks; cost implications of warm pools.

[00:00] Maya Chen: thanks everyone for joining, quick intros, I'm Maya AE at Redwood, with Diego our SE.
[00:12] Aisha Khan: hey thanks, Aisha here. We're evaluating options for inference for our customer-facing chat product, big focus on reliability and incidents because we have SLAs to our customers.
[00:21] Ben Marcus: Ben from infra, we'll be the ones operating network and peering.
[00:25] Rita Patel: Rita, security and compliance. Quick note, we'll need SOC2, audit logs, and SSO integration.
[00:32] Diego Ramos: great, high-level we'll talk about Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and how Redwood handles incident tolerance — routing policies, fallback models, multi-region, canary, etc.

[02:05] Aisha: our main pain is last year's outage where the vendor had a region issue and everything dropped, we had to degrade to a batch fallback which wasn't ideal. We're trying to understand how Redwood would route around a region outage and what guarantees we can expect.
[02:30] Maya: totally — two levers: routing + fallback. For routing we support multi-region routing policies by default at the control plane; you can set primary region and failover regions, and we do health checks and circuit breakers. For fallback we can transparently route to a compatible smaller model variant or a cheaper capacity tier.

[04:12] Ben: when you say health checks / circuit breaker, is that per-route or per-model? we need granularity so we don't fail all customers if one model misbehaves.
[04:23] Diego: per-route health checks with model-level granularity. We run periodic readiness probes, latency budgets; if a node or model variant exceeds error thresholds we trip a circuit and route to the next policy. There's also an option to do weighted traffic shifting — like 90/10 to a canary for a grace period.

[06:50] Aisha: can you fallback from a 32k context model to a 8k model? lots of our prompts rely on longer context, but in an incident we can accept degraded experience. How do you handle KV cache mismatch or truncated contexts?
[07:05] Diego: good question. For cross-model fallbacks we have prefix-aware fallbacks: we attempt to preserve as much of the prefix as possible; for large-context to small-context fallbacks we have configurable truncation policies and a cache reconciliation step. There are caveats — some structured outputs may break, we recommend tests in the pilot.

[09:40] Rita: from a security angle — if you reroute requests to another region or to Redwood-managed Dedicated capacity, is data encrypted at rest and in transit? Can we enforce KMS keys?
[09:55] Maya: yes, in Hosted everything is TLS in transit and encrypted at rest; we offer customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private. For Private we can integrate with your HSM/KMS. We'll attach SOC2+ISO docs after this call.

[12:10] Ben: what's the SLA on Hosted vs Dedicated? our contract requires at least 99.9 availability and predictable latency.
[12:22] Maya: Hosted standard SLA is 99.9; Dedicated can be 99.95 with reserved capacity and pre-warmed pools. For the strictest needs we recommend Dedicated or Private with reserved capacity and warm standbys. We can also offer credits for missed SLAs per the contract.

[14:35] Aisha: what about warm pools and pre-warmed GPUs? we saw long cold-start latency for some vendors.
[14:42] Diego: Dedicated supports warm pools: you can reserve X nodes that maintain model weights loaded and KV cache warming strategies. For Hosted we offer burst warm pools for committed tiers; warm pools increase cost but reduce p95/p99 cold-starts. We showed a sample TCO sheet in the doc pack.

[17:00] Ben: multi-region replication — if we have primary in us-west and failover in eu-west, how do you handle model versions and consistency? we don't want model diff surprises during failover.
[17:12] Diego: we recommend pinning model versions across regions; Redwood's deployment syncs artifacts and can promote the same model hash across regions. During POC we can validate model equivalence. For any rolling upgrade we support canary traffic to a percentage of users before full cutover.

[19:44] Aisha: in previous incidents our upstream provider started returning 5xx when overloaded and the retry storm made it worse. Do you do automatic backoff or load shedding?
[19:56] Diego: yes, request rate limiting, token-bucket based, client-side recommended backoffs, plus server side throttling and shedding for graceful degradation. We also support adaptive batching — during high load we increase batch sizes to improve throughput at cost of latency, configurable per-route.

[22:30] Rita: audit logs — we need request-level metadata and immutable logs for 90 days, and integration with our SIEM. Do you provide those?
[22:42] Maya: yes, Dedicated and Private include longer retention and S3-compatible audit exports; Hosted has 30 days by default, but enterprise add-on extends that. We'll send the compliance export documentation.

[25:15] Ben: curious about DNS-level vs in-app routing. If a whole cloud region is down, will DNS TTLs affect failover time?
[25:27] Diego: we use control-plane routing with health checks and an edge that can route by region; DNS TTL is one factor but our edge supports near-real-time failover using anycast and edge proxies to reduce flip times. Typical detectable failover is sub-30s for edge route changes, plus model cold-start if not pre-warmed.

[28:10] Aisha: can you do regional stickiness for data residency? Some users must be served from eu region only.
[28:20] Maya: yep — routing policies support hard regional constraints and tag-based routing. You can restrict particular customer traffic to eu regions and block failover to other regions if that violates residency requirements. That's often a config in Dedicated/Private; Hosted can support tenant-level residency if contracted.

[31:00] Ben: for POC can we simulate region outage and observe failover behavior?
[31:07] Diego: absolutely, we do chaos tests as part of scoping. In the POC we can run synthetic failovers and measure p50/p95/p99 and error rates — and validate that fallback model outputs are acceptable. We'll need your trace logs and representative prompts.

[34:20] Rita: encryption keys — if we use customer-managed KMS, during a failover to another region is key access available cross-region? HSM replication concerns.
[34:32] Diego: that's an operational constraint — if you require single-region KMS keys, you can disable cross-region failover for those workloads, or we can set up a Private deployment in the region. For Dedicated we can also integrate with your cross-region key replication plan. We'll document options.

[37:10] Aisha: how do you handle model fallbacks for structured responses / function calling? we use tool-calling heavily, and smaller models sometimes drop fields.
[37:25] Diego: function calling is best-effort during fallbacks; we provide schema validation and regression alerts. If a fallback produces malformed tool payloads we can route to a human-in-the-loop queue or to a specialized reranker. Part of the pilot is to define acceptance tests for outputs.

[40:00] Maya: quick note on cost — fallbacks to smaller models are cheaper but can change UX. We'll include examples in the TCO: warm pools + reserved capacity increase baseline cost but reduce tail latency.

[42:45] Ben: are there automated rollbacks if a canary shows degraded quality?
[42:52] Diego: yes, we support automatic rollback triggers based on latency/error thresholds or custom eval metrics tied to your prompt sets. Those integrate with the rollout policies in Console.

[45:10] Aisha: what about routing across Dedicated and Hosted? Ideally we want to use Hosted as a spillover when Dedicated is saturated but keep sensitive workloads on Dedicated. is that possible?
[45:22] Maya: yes — hybrid routing supported. You can set tiers: Dedicated preferred for tagged workloads, and Hosted as overflow. We do policy-based routing and can attach transformation rules and data-handling flags so PII isn't sent to Hosted unless allowed.

[48:00] Rita: compliance question — for fallback to Hosted, does data leave our VPC? we need to certify where data flows.

[48:10] Maya: if you use VPC peering and Private deployment we can ensure data stays on-prem or in your VPC. For Hosted fallback, by default requests go to Redwood control plane unless you configure strict VPC-only paths. We'll call out the data-plane flow in the doc we'll share.

[51:30] Ben: any limits on number of failover tiers? like primary -> warm Dedicated -> cold Dedicated -> Hosted -> smallest model?
[51:40] Diego: you can define multiple fallback tiers and ordering; the control plane evaluates in order with health checks and circuit breaker state. Each tier can have different model variants, quantization settings, etc.

[54:05] Aisha: one more — SLO targets: we're leaning toward 99.95 for availability and p99 latency under 800ms for short prompts. Is that realistic?
[54:17] Diego: for Dedicated with warm pools and reserved capacity that's achievable; Hosted for general-purpose may hit p99 ~1s depending on prompt length and batch behavior. We'll put benchmark numbers for similar workloads in the TCO/benchmarks doc.

[57:00] Rita: last compliance note — we need a detailed incident response runbook for failover scenarios and proof of regular DR drills.
[57:10] Maya: we'll include a sample runbook and propose quarterly DR exercises for the pilot.

[59:20] Wrap / recap: Maya: recap — Redwood will send SOC2/ISO docs, TCO spreadsheet, recommended canary configs, and propose POC scoping that includes simulated outages and synthetic traffic. Solaris to share p95/p99 traces and allowlist info.
[59:50] Aisha: thanks, that sounds good. We'll review and get back on dates for the scoping call.
[60:05] Diego: I'll draft a POC plan and share a calendar invite.
[60:15] End.

Notes: transcription contains occasional word errors and imperfect punctuation. Shared artifacts referenced: https://redwood.ai/docs/reliability (link), Hosted vs Dedicated TCO spreadsheet (link), SOC2 + ISO pack (link).
notes: Customer concerned about multi-region failover, data residency, and SLA. Redwood proposed Dedicated for 99.95 and warm pools; hosted as overflow. Actions: send docs and schedule POC.
